finding.title: Convert RewardMilestone/RewardUnlockRecord to @freezed data classes
finding.rule: Naming/placement (domain/state models are immutable @freezed classes; never hand-write ==/hashCode for data classes)
finding.why: Both classes are hand-written data holders with a hand-rolled copyWith/toJson/fromJson but no == / hashCode override at all, so they fall back to identity equality -- two RewardMilestones with identical field values are not `==`. Current call sites happen to compare by `.id` field rather than object equality (so no live bug was found), but this is fragile: any future code that puts RewardMilestone in a Set, uses List.contains, or relies on Riverpod .select()-style equality skipping would silently misbehave. The sibling model in the same feature (StreakRecoveryInfo) already follows the correct @freezed convention, showing the pattern is known and used elsewhere in this exact directory.
finding.recommendation: Convert RewardMilestone and RewardUnlockRecord to @freezed classes (keeping the existing toJson/fromJson as named factory/method overrides if the generated ones don't match the custom snake_case JSON shape).
acceptance_criteria: RewardMilestone and RewardUnlockRecord are @freezed with generated equality
Existing reward_milestone_test.dart suite passes unchanged (or updated only for the freezed toString/copyWith surface)

finding.title: Use ICU-parameterized l10n instead of raw 'label: value' string interpolation for chip/subtitle text
finding.rule: AX-2 (no hardcoded user-facing strings; everything via AppLocalizations/ARB with ICU placeholders)
finding.why: Both build a 'label: value' string by concatenating a localized label with a hardcoded ': ' separator and a raw number, rather than passing the value into an ICU-parameterized ARB string. The same feature already has the correct pattern for an almost identical 'reward cost' display (`l10n.pendingRedemptionsCost(redemption.pointsCost)` in parent_pending_redemptions_screen.dart, `l10n.achievementsMilestonePoints(...)` in achievement_tier_card.dart) -- these two sites are the odd ones out. Low practical impact (colon separators are largely locale-invariant) but genuinely inconsistent with the feature's own established i18n discipline.
finding.recommendation: Add/reuse an ICU-parameterized ARB entry (e.g. a 'labelWithValue' string) for both sites instead of raw interpolation.
acceptance_criteria: Both sites use an AppLocalizations method with a placeholder instead of raw string interpolation for the label/value pair

finding.title: Populate or delete the dead gamification.dart barrel file
finding.rule: Rule 2 (barrel is the only sanctioned re-export file) / dead code
finding.why: This 7-line file's own doc comment instructs other features to import it as the feature's public surface, but it contains zero `export` statements, and a repo-wide grep confirms zero files import it (the only match for the literal path string is the comment inside the file itself). Meanwhile 5 other features (dashboard, learning, notifications, sync, content_browsing) reach into features/gamification/** via 10+ direct deep imports of domain/models, domain/services, streak/*, and presentation/widgets paths instead. The file is not doing the job it documents itself as doing -- either because the codebase's barrel convention moved to providers.dart (per current coding-standards.md Rule 2) and this file is a stale leftover, or because populating it was simply never finished.
finding.recommendation: Either delete gamification.dart as stale scaffolding, or make it a real public surface (export the symbols the 10 external deep-import sites currently reach for) and redirect those imports through it -- consistent with whichever barrel filename convention (gamification.dart vs providers.dart) the team settles on.
acceptance_criteria: gamification.dart either exports real symbols with at least one external importer, or is removed from the tree

finding.title: streak_restorer.dart redefines kBulkPriorSentinelMs as a local magic number instead of importing the existing core constant
finding.rule: Evans (invariant enforced in one place) / Fowler (duplicated code, magic number)

evidence.quote:
// kBulkPriorSentinelMs (DateTime.utc(2000, 1, 1)); we define it locally to
    // avoid a core→features layering violation.

finding.why: The comment's stated reason is wrong: SchedulerEngine.kBulkPriorSentinelMs (the thing it says it's avoiding importing) lives in features/scheduler, not core, so importing it would be a cross-feature import (Rule 2), not a core→features violation (Rule 1) — and the correct fix was available anyway: lib/core/learning/completion_constants.dart already exports this exact constant from core, which features/ may freely import, and its own doc comment explicitly says it 'MUST be excluded from... streak calculations.' The sentinel (2000-01-01 UTC ms) now has three independent definitions (core/learning/completion_constants.dart, features/scheduler/domain/services/scheduler_engine.dart, and this file) that can silently diverge if any one is edited, corrupting bulk-prior filtering in exactly one of streak restore, points history, or scheduler completion detection without any test catching the mismatch.
finding.recommendation: Delete the local bulkPriorSentinelMs const and import kBulkPriorSentinelMs from core/learning/completion_constants.dart (a legal features→core import); fix the misleading comment.
acceptance_criteria: streak_restorer.dart imports and uses core's kBulkPriorSentinelMs; the local const is removed.
grep -rn '946684800000' lib/ returns exactly one hit (completion_constants.dart).

finding.title: Use directional layout APIs instead of EdgeInsets.only(left/right) and Positioned(right:) in gamification widgets
finding.why: tier_icon_box.dart's lock badge is pinned to the visual right/bottom corner with plain Positioned, which does not mirror under RTL — in Hebrew locale the badge renders on the leading (left) corner instead of the trailing corner. This is not hypothetical: the sibling file progress_summary_card.dart (same presentation/widgets/ directory) carries an explicit comment describing this exact bug ('With a plain Positioned(right:) it stayed on the visual right — the LEADING edge in Hebrew RTL — and collided with the right-aligned header text') that was fixed there with PositionedDirectional but never applied to tier_icon_box.dart. reward_config_header.dart's EdgeInsets.only(left:4, right:4) is currently symmetric so it renders identically in both directions today, but is one one-sided edit away from the same class of bug and still fails the AX-1 grep/lint intent.
finding.recommendation: Replace Positioned(right:, bottom:) with PositionedDirectional(end:, bottom:) in tier_icon_box.dart; replace EdgeInsets.only(left:, right:) with EdgeInsetsDirectional.only(start:, end:) in reward_config_header.dart.
acceptance_criteria: grep -rn 'Positioned(' lib/features/gamification/presentation/widgets/tier_icon_box.dart shows PositionedDirectional, not Positioned with right:/left:.
A widget test pumped under Locale('he')/TextDirection.rtl asserts the lock badge sits on the trailing (left-in-RTL) corner.
